mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A locally greater wind threat is evident in northwest Indiana.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: KLOT and TMDW/TORD radar velocity data suggest a locally greater wind threat developing in northwest Indiana. Two small bowing segments are evident with around 50 kt outbound velocities. Given the strong heating and large buoyancy ahead of these storms, they will likely pose a locally greater severe wind threat over the next 1-3 hours. Depending on the persistence of these storms, additional extensions of WW 547 may become necessary.

mesoscaleDiscussions.areas: Southeast Lower Michigan into northwest Ohio
mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The threat for wind damage will eventually spread eastward into parts of western Ohio and southeast Lower Michigan. A watch is possible for parts of these areas later this afternoon.

details.label: Areas affected
details.text: Southeast Lower Michigan into northwest Ohio

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Airmass destabilization continues in portions of northwest Ohio into southeast Lower Michigan. An upstream line of convection may impact portions of these areas later this afternoon into the evening. Cloud cover ahead of the convection has slowed the northward progress of the more favorable airmass and the northern portion of the convection has trended downward in the last hour. It is possible that the strongest activity may track farther south where buoyancy is much larger. The greatest risk for damaging winds will probably exist where dewpoints are 70+ F. However, at least isolated wind damage will remain possible along the instability gradient into the evening. A watch is possible for portions of these areas later this afternoon.
